rules.source: RFC 0005 §7.1 (round 2 review of host and tools, addition C)
rules.statement: A conversion never lets through a request 7.x refused, and never refuses silently what it cannot say: against what enforcement fills, a converted DENY is never narrower and a converted ALLOW never wider than its 7.x statement, except for a HEAD request where GET is allowed, which the conversion reports (PIP-18); what cannot be translated in its direction is rejected. A DENY is never dropped. On a part only 7.x filled (request.attributes.* but the gateway's route id, and resource.*), always absent in 8.0, a condition is a constant: one that holds on the absent value is rejected in both directions, one that does not is rejected in a DENY or negated in one, and narrows an ALLOW, recorded (NOT-IN-8.0).
guards: migrate:ConditionTranslatorTest#no row widens access against what enforcement fills
migrate:ConditionTranslatorTest#every row agrees with 7x on adversarial requests, never widening
migrate:ConditionTranslatorTest#a template on a part only 7x filled never holds as enforced, and is recorded
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a DENY on HEAD without GET is refused
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#an ALLOW on HEAD alone is dropped and recorded, one with others loses HEAD
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a DENY on method HEAD but not GET is refused, one that holds on GET is kept
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a DENY on a request attribute only 7x set is refused
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a condition that holds on the absent value of a part only 7x filled is refused in both directions
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a negated condition on a part only 7x filled is refused in a DENY
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#an ALLOW against a template on a part only 7x filled is recorded as never holding
migrate:Round2ConversionTest#a DENY with no action is rejected, an ALLOW with none is dropped

rules.statement: A conversion grants only the actions 7.x decided: an ALLOW of every 7.x action (the pattern `*`, `all` without methods, a `path` array holding `*`, or an array or composite holding one of them) is `http:*`, never `*`, so no converted ALLOW reaches a control-plane action (`cosec:*`) or the action of a check in code; a DENY of every 7.x action stays `*`, and the report records it (C7).
properties: migrate:ConvertedReachPropertyTest#no converted deployment permits an action outside http
guards: migrate:AllActionReachTest#a global allow of every action converts to no control-plane action
migrate:AllActionReachTest#an attachable allow of every action converts to no control-plane action
migrate:AllActionReachTest#a global allow of every action gives the platform tenant no control of the platform
migrate:AllActionReachTest#a DENY of every action still refuses everything, and is recorded
migrate:AllActionReachTest#a converted allow of every action publishes nothing through the control plane
migrate:MatcherTranslatorTest#every action is http star in an ALLOW and star in a DENY

rules.source: RFC 0007 §5.9 (RFC 0013 B4, the copies of a document)
rules.statement: `bootstrap`, forced or not, publishes the platform tenant's document with its binding added and everything else the document holds kept: its policies, its other bindings, its rate limits and its roles. Only the header (revision, publishedAt, provenance) and the bindings change, so a migration that converts 7.x roles into that document and then bootstraps does not lose them.
guards: migrate:BootstrapKeepsDocumentTest#bootstrap adds its binding and keeps the rest of the document
migrate:BootstrapKeepsDocumentTest#a forced bootstrap adds its binding and keeps the rest of the document

rules.source: RFC 0007 §5.8; design B of the back-references, beta.5 (#1729)
rules.statement: cosec-migrate repair-references converts a store written before 8.0.0-beta.5 and never replaces a back-reference set: it converts only a value CoCache reads in the old format, under a lease two runs share, adds and removes members otherwise, and removes the old document list last, only when nothing failed. A value no head touches stays in the old format and fails closed when a change touches it (CTL-42).
guards: migrate:LegacyConversionTest#a set is never replaced, so a member added after the conversion stays
migrate:MigrateMainTest#repair-references converts a store written before beta 5 and removes the old document list last
migrate:ReferenceRepairTest#a repair that fails part-way is reported, and the next run adds every missing member

rules.statement: cosec-migrate's report records each DENY and each rate limit rule that says something only an unmapped request has as a semantic change of its own, C9, beside C8: an http: action, an http:path: resource, or a condition on resource.id, action.verb or resource.var.* (7.x's request.path, request.method and request.path.var.*), in the statement or in its policy's condition. A route map takes the routes it maps out of that vocabulary, so such a DENY stops denying a mapped route and such a rule stops limiting it, which nothing at run time says. An ALLOW, a DENY of every action without a condition, and a condition on anything else are not recorded.
guards: migrate:UnmappedVocabularyTest#a DENY on a path records C9 for its http action and its http path resource
migrate:UnmappedVocabularyTest#a DENY of every action on request path or request method records C9, the path one with the encoding
migrate:UnmappedVocabularyTest#a policy condition on request path over a DENY records C9 at the policy condition
migrate:UnmappedVocabularyTest#a rate limit rule on a path records C9 as a rule that is no longer limited
migrate:UnmappedVocabularyTest#an ALLOW, a DENY of every action without a condition or on something else records no C9
